$comment: Intrvue.ai Medicine vertical — UK medical school interview map. Every record sourced from the institution's own admissions pages unless source_type says otherwise. Do not treat 'not published' as 'absent' — it means the school has not stated it.

meta.target_cycle: Applications autumn 2026 for 2027 entry; interviews Nov 2026 - Mar 2027

confidence_scale.HIGH: The institution's own page states it explicitly.
confidence_scale.MEDIUM: The institution's own page implies it, or states it for the most recent published cycle rather than 2027 entry.
confidence_scale.LOW: Third-party source only (Medical Schools Council, UCAS, reputable admissions site).
confidence_scale.UNCERTAIN: Sources conflict, or the field is unpublished anywhere.

meta.cycle_currency_warning: As at 2026-08-29 the majority of schools still display 2026-entry interview detail. Fields marked cycle_published:'2026' or earlier MUST be re-verified between September and November 2026. Build every field in this file as refreshable, not hard-coded.

schools.structure: Shortlisted on UCAT. MMI circuit Jan-Feb. Five minutes to answer questions at each station. Each station marked independently so one weak station does not carry over. Imperial publishes its topic list and its marking split but not the circuit logistics.
published_criteria: Understanding the role of a doctor
schools.scoring_note: Published rubric: 6 marks for content (what you say) and 4 marks for communication (how you say it) per station. 40% of every station is delivery.
schools.distinctive: One of only two schools publishing an explicit content/communication mark split. States the UCAS application is 'unlikely to be referred to during the interview stage' — personal-statement defence is low-yield here. Tells candidates questions 'could reflect a current news story'.
schools.changes: UCAT replaced BMAT from 2025 entry. No interview-format change published.
schools.confidence: HIGH on marking split, station length, topics, independent scoring; UNCERTAIN on station count, duration, delivery mode

schools.structure: MMIs run in a blended format mixing in-person and asynchronous interviews. GAMSAT or UCAT accepted. Work experience with service users is assessed at interview.
published_criteria: Commitment to medicine and understanding the role of a doctor
Potential to contribute to the medical school and the region
schools.distinctive: Candidates must prepare for two delivery modes in one circuit — live rapport and recorded monologue.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM

schools.structure: Up to 8 stations of 5 minutes, with 1 minute before each station to read the instructions; approximately 50 minutes total. Each station carries 2-3 questions. In person at the Rockefeller Building; rolling from December to end of March with no advantage to timing. Interviewers score independently on iPads.
schools.scientific_reasoning: partial (problem solving and reasoning ability assessed)
schools.ethics: not published as a station type
published_criteria: Academic curiosity and interest in healthcare
Motivation and understanding of the career
Team work, leadership and individual strengths
schools.scoring_note: Explicitly mapped to NHS values: putting patients first; respect and dignity; quality of care; compassion; improving health and wellbeing; inclusion.
schools.distinctive: Highest question density found anywhere — 2-3 questions inside a 5-minute station with only 1 minute of reading. Answers must be short. Personal statements are not scored for selection.
schools.changes: UCAT replaced BMAT from the 2024/25 cycle. No interview-format change published.
schools.confidence: HIGH

schools.structure: MMI of around 7 stations, each with a different member of staff asking one question. Interviews likely online, running November to May. No offers without interview. The A100 entry-requirements page describes no structure — station count and delivery come from King's own applicant FAQ PDFs.
published_criteria: General social and ethical issues, typically health-related
Suitability for the programme and the health professions
schools.distinctive: One question per station — very short-form. No contextual offers on A100; the contextual route is the separate A101 EMDP.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM on assessment focus; LOW on the 7-station online format (FAQ PDFs, not the course page)

schools.structure: Interviews conducted remotely; format not specified as MMI or panel. November to May. Strict fit-to-sit policy — mitigating circumstances affecting interview performance cannot be considered afterwards.
schools.distinctive: Gated eligibility: non-selective state education since 11, no prior degree, home fee status, plus a deprivation/care-experience indicator.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM

schools.structure: Remote panel of two interviewers using standardised scoring sheets. Home fee payers only. UCAT required.
schools.distinctive: Panel, not MMI — requires sustained conversational stamina rather than station reset.
schools.confidence: HIGH on panel format and remote delivery

schools.interview_type: panel (CONFLICTING — policy permits MMI or panel)
schools.structure: Selection-criteria page: online panels of two senior academic or clinical staff, sometimes with a lay selector, January to February. The 2026 Faculty admissions policy instead permits 'Multiple Mini Interviews (MMI) or panel interviews', in person or virtually. Both give the same six domains.
schools.delivery: CONFLICTING (course page: online; admissions policy: in-person or virtual)
published_criteria: Motivation and reality of a career in medicine or dentistry
schools.scoring_note: UCAT gate: overall in the fourth decile or above AND SJT Bands 1-3. SJT Band 4 ends the application at first shortlisting.
schools.distinctive: The clearest counter-example to Imperial: the panel has access to the UCAS application and may ask questions from it. Application-defence practice is high-yield here and low-yield at Imperial — this alone justifies a per-school flag in the product.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM overall; UNCERTAIN on interview type and delivery — sources conflict

schools.university: Queen Mary University of London (Malta campus)
schools.structure: Applied for directly to the University, not through UCAS, so it does not consume a UCAS choice. Online panel via Zoom. Candidates may not consult notes during the session.
schools.scoring_note: UCAT third decile and above; SJT Band 4 not considered.
schools.distinctive: Explicit no-notes rule — worth surfacing to users who practise with prompts on screen.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM

schools.university: City St George's, University of London
schools.structure: Six interview questions of around four minutes each. A station may involve answering a question, completing a practical task, or participating in a role play, for example dealing with a challenging situation. Each question is marked separately and independently.
published_criteria: Career motivation and commitment to the healthcare profession
Professional qualities — empathy, respect, dignity toward patients
Knowledge of current healthcare policies and research
schools.scoring_note: Publishes the line 'Often there is no right or wrong answer - the interviewers are assessing your ability to express your thinking.' Use this verbatim in product copy that resists model answers.
schools.distinctive: Stations may be practical tasks, not only speech. Four-minute stations reward concision.
schools.changes: For 2027 entry, UCAT SJT banding will be considered in decision-making. Institution flags possible MMI changes for the 2026 application cycle.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM — MMI confirmed on the 2027-entry course page; the six-question/four-minute detail comes from the institution's MMI guidance hub and is flagged as subject to change

schools.university: City St George's, University of London
schools.structure: MMI, usually in-person. Selection uses GAMSAT rather than UCAT. Institution-wide MMI guidance (six questions, ~4 minutes) presumed to apply but not restated on the A101 page.
schools.distinctive: GAMSAT-gated; eligible sittings for the 2027 cycle run March 2025 to September 2026, highest score used.
schools.changes: Flagged as possibly changing for the 2027 application cycle.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM on MMI and in-person; LOW on station count and length

schools.structure: Asynchronous virtual MMI. Candidates receive a link and have five days to complete the interview at a time of their choosing, working through stations in any order. Six stations, each allowing 2 minutes to read the scenario and 5 minutes to complete the task. Every station is blueprinted to Good Medical Practice. Brunel states explicitly it will not ask academic questions. Practice questions with automated feedback are provided beforehand.
schools.independently_scored: sum of marks; no per-station minimum
published_criteria: Six mini-interview stations, each designed to assess a different attribute aligned with Good Medical Practice
schools.scoring_note: SJT Band 4 not accepted. Candidates ranked by total vMMI score against an annually agreed cut-off.
schools.distinctive: The single biggest format outlier in the UK. No interviewer, no rapport, no follow-up — a recorded monologue against a timer. Practice for Brunel is a fundamentally different skill and is the one format where an AI product's asynchronous recording mode is an exact simulation rather than an approximation.
schools.changes: Earlier documentation described live virtual rooms; treat the asynchronous model as current.
schools.confidence: HIGH on format, station count, timing, five-day window; UNCERTAIN on total duration (40 vs 45 minutes across two current Brunel pages)

schools.structure: Six short stations covering data handling, problem analysis, situational judgement, roleplay, task, and values-based, each 7 minutes with 3-minute intervals, PLUS a single 40-minute group station in which candidates are assessed individually. Roughly 60+ minutes excluding intervals. International (Group E) applicants take 3 short stations plus the group station, remotely.
schools.delivery: hybrid (in-person for most; remote for international)
published_criteria: A realistic and committed attitude to medical training
Ability to communicate effectively and to work well in a team
schools.scoring_note: Casper (Acuity Insights) additionally required for Groups C, D and E, used to rank rather than threshold. No predicted grades used in selection; relative attainment against school averages replaces absolute grades at shortlisting.
schools.distinctive: The most content-diverse single circuit in the UK — data, roleplay, task, values and a 40-minute group exercise in one sitting. Also the only school in the set to warn that commercial preparation 'might be less useful' and that school-organised coaching may be 'positively disadvantageous', and to require an NDA. Treat that stance as a marketing constraint, not just a curiosity.
schools.changes: KMMS explicitly states it does not commit to the same number or type of stations for the coming cycle.
schools.confidence: HIGH for the published 2025-26 structure, explicitly labelled by KMMS as subject to change

schools.structure: Virtual MMI cycle lasting under one hour. Each station independently marked against agreed criteria and assessing a specific competency, staffed by academic and clinical professionals. Candidates ranked on total MMI score.
schools.scoring_note: GAMSAT required for most; UCAT accepted only from Biochemistry, Biology, Biomedical Science, Chemistry or Natural Sciences degrees.
schools.distinctive: SURREY HAS NO A100. If the product lists Surrey as an undergraduate option, that is a factual error to correct before launch.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM

schools.structure: Interviewed by two colleges — one chosen or allocated, one randomly assigned. Each panel has at least two academics and at least one practising clinician. Described as academic conversations about the subject, similar to a short tutorial. Interviewers are not aware of applicants' UCAT scores.
schools.application_questioning: partial (university-wide guidance says discussion may draw on the personal statement)
schools.independently_scored: two colleges assess independently against common criteria
published_criteria: Empathy: ability and willingness to imagine the feelings of others and understand the reasons for the views of others
Motivation: a reasonably well-informed and strong desire to practise medicine
Communication: ability to make knowledge and ideas clear using language appropriate to different audiences, including patients
Capacity for sustained and intense work
Intellectual curiosity: keenness to understand the reason for observations; depth; tendency to look for meaning; enthusiasm and curiosity in science
Communication skills: willingness and ability to express clearly and effectively; ability to listen; compatibility with tutorial format
schools.scoring_note: Selection criteria are common to all colleges. NHS Constitution values are named in the criteria.
schools.distinctive: Interviewers blinded to UCAT — unique in this dataset. The personal-characteristics criteria list is as long as the academic one, which contradicts the common assumption that Oxford is purely academic.
schools.confidence: HIGH on delivery, panel composition, two-college structure and criteria; MEDIUM on number and length of interviews

schools.structure: Normally more than one interview; typically two at each college, and every candidate is interviewed at two colleges — so typically four interviews. Panels include college tutors and clinical tutors.
schools.scoring_note: Selection draws on the application form and UCAS information, referees' statements, interview performance and UCAT.
schools.distinctive: Four interviews is the highest interview count of any non-MMI route in the dataset — stamina and consistency across repeated academic conversation.
schools.confidence: HIGH on number of interviews, delivery and dates; LOW on content detail

schools.structure: Interviews held by individual colleges. Most applicants have 1-2 interviews totalling 35 minutes to an hour; some have 3-4. Candidates discuss topics with two or three interviewers and apply knowledge to new situations. Cambridge requires at least two interviews per medical applicant with at least one current practitioner involved. Winter-pool candidates may get an additional January interview at a different college.
schools.delivery: CONFLICTING — college-dependent; the university publishes a per-college table rather than a course-level answer
schools.numeracy_data: not published as a discrete task
schools.application_questioning: partial (may cover recent school topics or the personal statement)
published_criteria: Scientific and related competencies — sixth-form Chemistry, Biology, Maths and Physics; application of knowledge to novel scenarios; lateral thinking and conceptual flexibility; observation and hypothesis generation
Personal qualities — emotional maturity and motivation, listening, empathy, communication, team-working, capacity to handle stressful situations
Professional and career considerations — substantiated motivation, realistic understanding, ethical reasoning, social awareness
schools.scoring_note: For 2027 entry Cambridge uses the overall cognitive UCAT subtest score and will NOT use the situational judgement score. No minimum UCAT threshold.
schools.distinctive: The most concretely specified scientific-reasoning expectation in the UK — named A-level subjects applied to novel problems. No pre-submitted written work required; Medicine is absent from the 2027-entry at-interview assessment list.
schools.changes: 2027 entry: SJT dropped from consideration; overall cognitive score used.
schools.confidence: HIGH on UCAT policy, two-interview minimum and criteria; MEDIUM on duration and number; UNCERTAIN on delivery mode

schools.structure: Assessment through a mixture of academic record, UCAT and interviews. No A101-specific interview-format detail published. Delivered through a restricted set of colleges.
schools.scoring_note: 2027 entry: overall cognitive UCAT score used; SJT not used; no minimum threshold.
schools.confidence: HIGH on UCAT policy; absent on interview format

schools.structure: Six stations, each with a different interviewer. Five minutes at each station with 1.5 minutes preparation. Questions are written against the Medical Schools Council statement on core values and attributes. Interview score and UCAT score are weighted equally to rank applicants for offers.
published_criteria: Mapped to the Medical Schools Council statement on the core values and attributes needed to study medicine
schools.scoring_note: Interview and UCAT weighted equally at the offer stage.
schools.distinctive: One of the clearest statements that stations are written directly against the MSC attributes — makes MSC-mapped rubrics directly defensible for this school.
schools.confidence: HIGH on structure; absent on content detail

schools.structure: Same format as A100 — six stations, five minutes each, 1.5 minutes preparation, on campus. GAMSAT preferred; UCAT accepted only from recent biomedical degree holders.
schools.confidence: HIGH on structure; UNCERTAIN on course code

schools.structure: Six stations, each seven minutes with one minute reading of instructions outside the station. Some stations involve actors in scenario-based interaction. Each station is scored across three domains out of five each — 15 per station, 90 overall. In person at Chelmsford.
schools.application_questioning: partial — PS not directly used but candidates should be prepared to discuss aspects of it
schools.scoring_note: The clearest published per-station rubric in the dataset: three equally weighted domains per station, 15 per station, 90 total. Directly convertible into a scoring schema.
schools.distinctive: Confirms actors. The three-domain rubric separates content quality from evidenced attribute from communication — a better model for our own scoring than most schools publish.
schools.confidence: HIGH

schools.structure: About an hour in total. On-campus A100 candidates rotate through 7 stations of roughly 10 minutes, one of which is a simple numeracy station requiring no medical knowledge and no calculator. Online candidates take 6 stations of 7 minutes plus a separate numeracy station. Written instructions sit outside each station with time to read.
schools.delivery: hybrid by cohort (face-to-face for Home, online for International/A199)
published_criteria: Ability to show empathy and compassion
schools.scoring_note: The numeracy station carries a pass-mark threshold — a hurdle, not a contribution to a total. Mental arithmetic, no calculator, no medical knowledge.
schools.distinctive: The only school in the dataset publishing numeracy as a threshold hurdle. Ten-minute stations are the longest standard MMI stations found and support genuine follow-up questioning.
schools.changes: Not stated; school notes it regularly reviews its interview process.
schools.confidence: HIGH on delivery, numeracy and criteria; MEDIUM on station count and length (candidate page labelled to an earlier cycle)

schools.interview_type: MMI-style scenario circuit (Nottingham calls them scenarios)
schools.structure: Six scenarios lasting up to one hour in total, including at least one role-play scenario. Usually December to February. Assessment based on Medical Schools Council guidance on communication, professional issues and respect for patients and colleagues. Personal statements are not scored and are reviewed only after interview.
schools.delivery: hybrid by fee status for 2027 entry (in-person for Home, online via Teams for International)
published_criteria: An understanding of professional issues such as teamwork
Respect for patients and the contribution of those working in professions allied to medicine
schools.scoring_note: UCAT SJT Band 1-3 required to progress.
schools.distinctive: Guarantees at least one roleplay in every circuit — a concrete argument for our roleplay engine being core, not optional.
schools.changes: 2026 entry was all online via Teams; 2027 entry moves Home applicants to in-person.
schools.confidence: HIGH

schools.structure: Six scenarios, up to one hour, including at least one role play — the same model as A100. Interviews 9 and 11 December 2026 for 2027 entry.
schools.delivery: in-person for Home; online via Teams for International
schools.distinctive: Largest cycle-on-cycle change found anywhere in the dataset.
schools.changes: 2026 entry used GAMSAT and all-online interviews; 2027 entry uses UCAT with in-person interviews for Home applicants.
schools.confidence: HIGH on the 2027 test change, delivery and dates; MEDIUM on scenario detail

schools.structure: Seven MMI stations, each scored across several domains, giving a total interview score out of 70. In person at the Brayford Campus. UCAT contributes to a Combined Academic Score of up to 30 points; SJT Band 4 excluded.
published_criteria: Evidence of skills and attributes appropriate to a career in Medicine
Insight into a range of topics related to working as a doctor
schools.scoring_note: Total interview score out of 70; each station scored across several domains.
schools.distinctive: Lincoln now runs its own MBChB at Brayford; the historic joint Nottingham-Lincoln arrangement is not described on current pages. GMC status: under review, not yet fully approved.
schools.confidence: HIGH on station count, scoring total, delivery; absent on timings

schools.structure: Three stages. Stage One academic screening. Stage Two a computer-based Multiple Mini Assessment; exceptionally high performers may receive an offer at this stage. Stage Three the MMI/OSSE — a circuit of tasks testing analysis, interpretation and judgement related to Good Medical Practice. All conducted online.
schools.scientific_reasoning: computer-based aptitude assessment at Stage Two
published_criteria: Tasks intended to test abilities related to Good Medical Practice
Judge personal attributes relating to suitability for practice as a doctor
schools.scoring_note: Performance at each station scored against a checklist defined in advance; total cumulated and applicants ranked.
schools.distinctive: No UCAT requirement; an in-house computer-based assessment plays that role. January 2027 intake. Fees £41,500/yr UK. Low priority for a UK-market product given fee level and applicant volume.
schools.confidence: HIGH on the three-stage model and scoring method; absent on station detail

schools.structure: Six or seven stations described as a mix of interviews, role-play and calculation tasks. Named stations: Critical Thinking; Commitment and Insight into Medicine; Dealing with Personal and Ethical Challenges; Professionalism; Data Interpretation and Debate; Interaction in Healthcare Setting (role-play); Calculation Station (computer-based). Eight minutes per station inclusive of two minutes' preparation. International applicants sit a minimum of two stations online plus a separate calculations assessment.
schools.delivery: hybrid (in-person for Home; online via Zoom for International)
schools.scientific_reasoning: critical thinking and data interpretation only
schools.application_questioning: partial — PS not scored but evidence of commitment required; work experience discussed at the Commitment and Insight station
published_criteria: Dealing with Personal and Ethical Challenges
schools.scoring_note: All MMI stations and the UCAT SJT component are equally weighted. SJT Band 1 = max, Band 2 = 2/3, Band 3 = 1/3, Band 4 = 0. Pre-interview scoring is 45% academic, 40% UCAT, 15% contextual.
schools.distinctive: The most fully specified station blueprint published by any UK medical school, and the only one naming a computer-based calculation station AND a professional role-player station AND a debate station. This is the single best template for a university-specific practice mode.
schools.changes: Interview page is labelled 2026 entry; entry-requirements page is 2027 entry. Re-verify station list in autumn 2026.
schools.confidence: HIGH for 2026-entry structure; MEDIUM that it carries unchanged to 2027 entry

schools.structure: Online MMI, December to March. Candidates rotate through stations assessing named attributes; medical knowledge is explicitly not tested. Scored per station then aggregated. 2025-entry statistics report MMI scores out of 50 with a maximum of 10 at each station, implying five stations for that cycle.
schools.application_questioning: not published (MSC: may be used during interviews)
published_criteria: Being able to lead as well as follow
Knowing your limitations and knowing when to ask for help
schools.scoring_note: 10 marks per station; 50 total (2025 entry).
schools.distinctive: Publishes 'Knowing your limitations and knowing when to ask for help' as an explicit assessed attribute — this is the competence-boundary behaviour our scoring must reward and is rarely named this directly.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM; station count inferred from 2025 scoring data

schools.structure: Six MMI stations of approximately 10 minutes. In person at the Junction building, main campus, 15-18 December 2026 for 2027 entry. An online session runs 13 January 2027 for international applicants — same six stations, 5-minute technical check beforehand, approximately 80 minutes total. Each station observed and scored by trained assessors drawn from medical professionals, academics, current students and lay people.
schools.delivery: hybrid (in-person main cohort; online session for international)
schools.scoring_note: Warwick runs no undergraduate A100.
schools.distinctive: Ten-minute stations plus published 2027 dates make this one of the few schools where a fully accurate timed simulation is possible today.
schools.confidence: HIGH on station count, length, delivery and dates; absent on content

schools.interview_type: two separate structured interviews (not a station circuit)
schools.structure: Two separate 15-minute interviews, usually about two hours apart on the same day, delivered online via Microsoft Teams. One to two days beforehand applicants are sent the professionalism section of the GMC's 'Achieving Good Medical Practice: Guidance for Medical Students' plus a short case study specific to their session, and are told they are not expected to memorise anything from these texts.
schools.application_questioning: PS scored at shortlisting; interview use not stated
published_criteria: Awareness of the doctor's role in healthcare teams and society
Engagement with people needing care or support
schools.scoring_note: Offer decision based on interview performance; ties broken by UCAT.
schools.distinctive: The only school issuing prepared reading material in advance. Practice for Keele needs a pre-read attachment and a discussion-of-supplied-text mode — cheap to build, and nobody else offers it.
schools.changes: Cycle labelling conflicts: Keele's how-to-apply page still says September 2025 entry; MSC lists the same two-interview online-hybrid format for 2027 entry.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM — format HIGH from Keele's own page but the page is cycle-stale; 2027 applicability from MSC only

schools.university: University of Worcester (Three Counties Medical School)
schools.interview_type: hybrid panel + MMI (LOW confidence — MSC only)
schools.structure: Worcester's own pages describe the selection stages — UCAT or GAMSAT ranking, then CASPer for shortlisted applicants, then interview — but do not publish the interview format. MSC states the interview is in-person and combines a traditional panel with MMI stations, with CASPer incorporated into the MMI stage.
schools.ethics: CASPer assesses situational judgement and professionalism
schools.scoring_note: Shortlisted applicants typically above 50 on GAMSAT or 1870 on UCAT; no hard cut-off.
schools.distinctive: NO A100 — graduate entry only. One of two schools using CASPer. GMC status: under review.
schools.confidence: LOW on interview format; HIGH on selection stages

schools.structure: Six MMI stations, in person, totalling approximately one and a half hours. Each station observed and scored by two trained assessors drawn from medical professionals, academics, current students and lay people. Stations designed to assess against GMC Good Medical Practice. No place offered without interview.
published_criteria: Assessed against GMC Good Medical Practice
schools.scoring_note: Two assessors per station.
schools.distinctive: NO A100 — graduate entry only. NOT YET FULLY GMC-APPROVED for award; progressing through approval with Warwick Medical School as contingency partner. Flag this in product copy.
schools.confidence: HIGH on station count, duration, delivery, scoring; absent on content

schools.structure: Multi-station MMI held between December and April. Interviews at the Preston campus include a guided tour of facilities. MSC records the format as both in-person and online MMIs. No station count, length or content published on the university's own pages.
schools.delivery: hybrid (in-person Preston confirmed; online per MSC)
schools.application_questioning: MSC only: used during the interview
schools.distinctive: Home/UK recruitment severely restricted — 'a very limited number of places available for UK students'. Weakest case in the dataset for building UK-market practice content. Note the rebrand to University of Lancashire; do not confuse with Lancaster Medical School.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM on format and delivery; absent on all content fields

schools.structure: Four-stage process — academic screening, UCAT ranking with an annually varying threshold, interview, scoring — but both the interview format and the scoring methodology are marked 'Details TBC' on the 2027-entry page. MSC confirms MMI. A 2020 admissions policy (still hosted) gives a competency list and per-station scoring but no station count, length or delivery mode.
published_criteria: Motivation for wanting to join the MBChB Programme
schools.scoring_note: UCAT SJT Band 4 = automatic rejection. Individual station scores are not released to applicants.
schools.distinctive: UK applicants only. The 2020 competency list explicitly names 'Awareness of current health challenges' and 'Prioritization/decision making' — useful evidence that current affairs and prioritisation are genuinely assessed, but the document is six years old.
schools.changes: Interview format explicitly TBC for 2027 entry — re-check in autumn 2026.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM on MMI type and process; LOW/DATED on the competency list (May 2020 policy)

schools.structure: Five MMI stations, eight minutes each, with two-minute gaps. Each station is marked by a separate interviewer; the starting station is allocated randomly. Candidates choose online (Zoom) or in-person, with limited places in each on a first-come-first-served basis and identical assessment either way. Interviewers include simulated patients and patient/lay representatives.
schools.scoring_note: No reading or writing component at any station — everything is spoken, cold.
schools.distinctive: Explicitly names 'contemporary medical knowledge' as an assessed criterion — direct evidence for the tester's complaint that current affairs is missing from our bank. Uses simulated patients as interviewers. The only school offering candidates a free choice of delivery mode.
schools.confidence: HIGH

schools.structure: MMI stated for 2027 entry, described as compatible with Values Based Recruitment and the Selecting for Excellence report. Home and Irish applicants travel to campus; international applicants take an equivalent online MMI. Structure and criteria likely the same for all A100 applicants. No station-level detail published.
published_criteria: Awareness of and insight into a career in healthcare
Critical, coherent, and informative approach to verbal and written communication
schools.changes: 2026 and 2027 supplements materially identical on interview format.
schools.confidence: HIGH on format; absent on all station detail

schools.structure: A101 route exists and graduate applicants must sit GAMSAT. The admissions process page indicates A101 uses the same MMI process as A100. No A101-specific detail published.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM on existence and MMI format; absent on detail

schools.structure: Online MMI via Microsoft Teams. Applicants complete a number of stations assessing skills, values and attributes required to study and practise medicine. Each station assessed by trained interviewers and scored against clear criteria, combined into an overall score. Interviewers include university staff, NHS clinicians, public representatives and medical students.
published_criteria: Skills, values and attributes required to study and practise medicine successfully
schools.scoring_note: References GMC 'Achieving good medical practice: guidance for medical students'.
schools.distinctive: States the personal statement is an opportunity to prepare for the types of questions asked at interview — application-based questioning is in scope here. NOTE: an archived Lancaster policy describing 12-15 stations plus a 20-minute group task is from the BMAT era (2016 entry) and is superseded — do not use it.
schools.confidence: HIGH on delivery and scoring; absent on station count and timings

schools.structure: Eight stations, six minutes each, with two minutes outside each station to read materials and make notes. One interviewer per station reads instructions aloud; candidates may ask for questions to be rephrased. Face-to-face on campus (online for overseas). Interviews 4-6 January 2027.
schools.scoring_note: Marked against pre-determined, standardised scoring scales. Critically: 'The decision to make an offer after interview depends entirely on performance at interview, not on predicted or achieved academic performance, or UCAT scores.'
schools.distinctive: The highest-stakes interview in the dataset — UCAT and academics govern shortlisting only, and the offer rests entirely on interview performance. Explicitly states the interview does not test clinical or scientific knowledge, and explicitly tells candidates to keep up to date with health and social care headlines.
schools.confidence: HIGH

schools.route: undergraduate (widening participation gateway — NOT graduate entry)
schools.structure: Same MMI format as A100 — eight stations, six minutes, two minutes' reading. Face-to-face, 4-5 January 2027. Restricted to UK applicants meeting contextual criteria. Graduate applicants are not accepted.
schools.scoring_note: Offers depend entirely on interview performance.
schools.distinctive: Leeds A101 is a Gateway Year, not graduate entry. Leeds has no graduate-entry medicine course — a common product data error.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM (station detail inherited from the shared Medicine/Gateway MMI page)

schools.structure: Home applicants attend in-person MMIs covering eight assessed sections; international applicants take online panel interviews. Each section scored on a five-point scale (5 Excellent, 4 Good, 3 Satisfactory, 2 Borderline, 1 Unsatisfactory). The UCAT SJT band is converted to the same five-point scale by quartile, giving 45 points total. Panels draw on medical educators, hospital doctors, GPs, biomedical scientists, senior nurses, pharmacists, medical students and lay people.
schools.numeracy_data: not published as such — 'Information processing' is a named section
schools.scoring_note: Published prioritisation rule: 'Applicants who achieve a score of three or better in every MMI section and the SJT will be prioritised in the ranking process.' This is a per-station floor, not a total — the single most important scoring design fact in the dataset.
schools.distinctive: The most granular published scoring model in the UK: named sections, an explicit five-point descriptor scale, a 45-point total including SJT, and a per-section floor. Uniquely states it does not read or score personal statements. Also uniquely has a 'Knowledge of Sheffield' section — the only school where course-specific research is directly scored. Notes and materials are not permitted during the interview.
schools.changes: UCAT threshold restated from 2430/3600 to 1800/2700 following the change in UCAT format.
schools.confidence: HIGH

schools.interview_type: MMI hybrid — includes a group exercise and a video-based individual scenario
schools.structure: Home fee status, in person: four stations — a group exercise (22 points), two mini-interviews (17 points each), and an individual scenario station (17 points), 90 points total. The group exercise takes up to 10 candidates, is facilitated by problem-based learning tutors and scored by the tutor plus an observing medical student. Each mini-interview has two interviewers scoring independently and asks two questions, with 5 minutes' thinking time before each. The individual scenario station plays a pre-recorded video through over-ear headphones with questions at two points during and once after.
schools.roleplay: yes — pre-recorded video with character interaction, not a live actor
published_criteria: Understanding of the values in the NHS Constitution
Personal qualities — empathy, tolerance of ambiguity and resilience
schools.scoring_note: Overseas structure differs: 4 stations (three mini-interviews at 15 points each, individual scenario 15, group exercise 15), 60 points total, one question per station, 2 minutes' thinking time, group of up to 6.
schools.distinctive: The only school publishing a live group exercise as a scored station with published point weights, and the only one using a pre-recorded video scenario over headphones. Five minutes of thinking time per question is by far the most generous preparation in the dataset — a completely different answer-construction skill from UCL's one minute.
schools.confidence: HIGH

schools.structure: Home applicants take MMIs on campus; each station scored by an individual selector. Selectors have no access to the applicant's personal statement or reference. The UCAT SJT band is folded into the final interview score with the same weighting as one MMI station (Band 1 = 5 points, Band 2 = 3, Band 3 = 1). Final ranking is 50% academic screen, 50% interview.
published_criteria: Motivation and commitment to be a doctor
schools.scoring_note: SJT band weighted as one full MMI station — a genuine post-interview UCAT use, unlike most schools.
schools.distinctive: One station involves a role-play scenario (2025-entry page). Selectors blinded to the application.
schools.confidence: HIGH on scoring, UCAT use and domains (2027 policy); MEDIUM on station count and length (2025-entry figure, not restated for 2027)

schools.structure: Graduate and international applicants are interviewed by a panel of two interviewers, on campus or remotely, rather than by MMI. The panel asks a comparable set of questions to the MMI. Each selector scores separately. Same SJT-band weighting and 50:50 academic/interview ranking as A100.
schools.distinctive: Same content, different container — the clearest single case in the dataset that a school can run identical domains through a panel and an MMI. Supports building content domain-first and rendering it into a format at runtime.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM

schools.structure: A series of short interview stations. For 2027/28 entry the course page states interviews take place in the week commencing 7 December 2026, in person. Shortlisting combines academic qualifications, UCAT, and an 'interview selection tool' — a reflective survey on work experience. All interviews completed before any offer decisions.
schools.delivery: CONFLICTING — course page says in-person; School of Medicine help page says online MMIs on Microsoft Teams
schools.application_questioning: not published (separate reflective work-experience survey used at shortlisting)
schools.scoring_note: UCAT: top 8 deciles with SJT Bands 1-3.
schools.distinctive: Uses a separate reflective work-experience survey at shortlisting — the only school in the dataset doing so. Worth a content note for users applying here.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM on MMI format and dates; UNCERTAIN on delivery mode

schools.university: Pears Cumbria School of Medicine (Imperial / University of Cumbria)
schools.structure: MMIs in person at the Carlisle campus; Imperial's course page describes a blended format mixing in-person and asynchronous interviews. Six assessment domains published. Candidates without local links are assessed on their understanding of and interest in improving health outcomes for the people of Cumbria.
published_criteria: Commitment to medicine and understanding the role of a doctor
Potential to contribute to the medical school and the region
schools.scoring_note: GAMSAT or UCAT. Home students only; 2:1 in biosciences or an allied healthcare degree.
schools.distinctive: GRADUATE ENTRY ONLY — there is no undergraduate A100. Explicitly assesses regional commitment to Cumbria, which is a genuinely school-specific content requirement. GMC status: under review via Imperial.
schools.changes: Both school pages still display the closed 2026 cycle; 2027 recruitment confirmed via UCAS only.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM

schools.structure: Six stations, each assessed by three assessors, delivered remotely over Zoom. Candidates meet six assessors in total, in two groups of three, each group marking three stations. Station scores combined into a total. Photo ID required; no notes, books, devices or AI tools permitted.
schools.ethics: candidates directed to read GMC guidance for medical students
published_criteria: Skills and attributes appropriate to a career in medicine
Insight into a range of topics related to a career in medicine
schools.scoring_note: Three assessors per station is the highest assessor density in the dataset. MSC's 2027-entry tool entry reads: 'Applicants move around six MMI stations lasting 5 mins each.'
schools.distinctive: Explicitly bans AI tools during the interview. Thirty minutes total makes this the shortest full circuit found — concision is the dominant demand.
schools.changes: Personal statement no longer used as a weighted selection component (undated).
schools.confidence: MEDIUM — structure HIGH but published for 2026 entry; MSC corroborates for 2027

schools.structure: Bristol's interview page covers A100 and Gateway jointly, implying the same six-station remote structured format. No A108-specific interview specification published.
schools.scoring_note: UCAT bursaries available to cover test cost.
schools.distinctive: Eligibility by WP criteria — designated schools/colleges, 3+ months care experience, or free school meals.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM — inherited from the shared A100/Gateway page

schools.structure: MMI format confirmed for 2027 entry; delivery may take place either in person or online — mode not fixed. Shortlisted applicants interviewed between December and March; approximately 700 interviewed including ~30 international. Offers late February/early March.
schools.delivery: hybrid (undecided — 'may take place either in person or online')
published_criteria: Non-academic qualities such as communication skills, reflectiveness and empathy
schools.distinctive: Exeter and Plymouth have clearly diverged since the Peninsula split and are no longer interchangeable for preparation. A legacy Exeter page states 4 stations for 2024 entry — treat as unconfirmed.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM on format and delivery; absent on structure

schools.course: BMBS Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery
schools.structure: Five stations assessed by four different interviewers, approximately 55 minutes in total. Panels comprise clinicians, academics, medical students, healthcare professionals and members of the public. Interviews explore attitudes, outlook and way of thinking rather than medical or scientific knowledge. Scored on a numerical scale plus a red-flag section (Yes/No) for unsuitable behaviour or statements.
schools.delivery: online (Zoom) — 'committed to online interviews for the current admission cycle'
schools.scoring_note: Explicit red-flag section scored Yes/No for unsuitable behaviour or statements, separate from the numerical scale. This is the only published confirmation that UK schools score red flags as a distinct binary — our scoring model should mirror it.
schools.distinctive: 'Impact of illness' as a named assessed quality is unusual and content-relevant: it points at patient-experience understanding rather than clinical knowledge. Explicitly does not consider personal statements or work experience when selecting for interview.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM — station count and duration anchored to the 2024 cycle; online delivery confirmed for the current cycle

schools.interview_type: selection day — interview plus group task (NOT MMI)
schools.structure: Southampton runs a selection day, not an MMI circuit: the process includes an interview and a group task. Attendance must be in person — 'due to the format of our selection process we do not offer online alternatives.' Selection days run January to end of February. Offers made on interview performance, with UCAT used only to break ties.
published_criteria: Have reflected on and learnt from life experiences
Are able to interact successfully with others
Can demonstrate an understanding of the values of the NHS Constitution
schools.scoring_note: Offers made on selection-day performance; UCAT is the tiebreak only.
schools.distinctive: The clearest format outlier among large schools: no station circuit at all. Explicitly draws on application content at interview AND runs a formal group task AND names the NHS Constitution. A candidate preparing for Southampton and for Bristol is preparing for two different exams.
schools.confidence: HIGH on format, delivery and criteria; absent on timings

schools.course: BMBS Medicine BM6 Widening Participation (6 years)
schools.interview_type: selection day — interview plus group task
schools.structure: Same selection-day model as BM5. Applicants meeting academic and eligibility criteria are ranked by UCAT and the top number invited. Invitations give 2-3 weeks' notice. Decisions by end of March.
schools.confidence: HIGH on format and delivery

schools.course: BMBS Medicine BM4 Graduate Entry (4 years)
schools.interview_type: selection day — interview plus group task
schools.structure: Same selection-day format as BM5/BM6. Applicants ranked by UCAT; offers on selection-day performance with UCAT as tiebreak. In-person attendance mandatory. Some interview places reserved for Southampton graduates. 2027 dates announced autumn 2026.
schools.confidence: HIGH on format and delivery; MEDIUM on BM4-specific differences

schools.structure: Five discussion stations of 10 minutes each with 90-second breaks, approximately one hour total. Each discussion assessed and scored separately, marked out of 20, giving a global score out of 100. For 2027 entry candidates choose in-person (early December or early January) or virtual Zoom (late January or early February). Photo ID mandatory or the interview is forfeited.
schools.delivery: hybrid (applicant chooses in-person or Zoom, tied to the calendar slot)
published_criteria: Each element rated Excellent, Good, Satisfactory, Borderline or Poor before a score is issued
schools.scoring_note: Five-band descriptor scale then a numeric score out of 20 per station. Advises candidates to reflect on work experience referring to the skills and values attributes needed to study medicine.
schools.distinctive: 'BSMS does not use personal statements at any point during the admissions process' — the most categorical statement of its kind in the dataset. Ten-minute discussion stations with no preparation time are a distinct demand: sustained conversation, not a prepared answer.
schools.confidence: HIGH on dates, delivery and PS policy; MEDIUM on station timings (guidance PDF last updated October 2022)

schools.structure: A series of short, carefully timed stations rotated in turn, with themed questions. For 2027 entry delivery is split by fee status: in person for home applicants, online for overseas. Candidates may interview through the medium of Welsh or bilingually on scheduled dates. No offer without interview; invitations targeted by mid-December.
schools.delivery: hybrid by fee status (in-person Home; online Overseas) for 2027 entry
schools.application_questioning: CONFLICTING — course page tells applicants to demonstrate healthcare awareness in the personal statement; the 2026 school admissions policy scores applications on achieved qualifications only
published_criteria: Understanding of a career in medicine
schools.scoring_note: MMIs assess ability to think quickly and adapt to novel scenarios, awareness of professional issues, critical appraisal, communication, and personal qualities.
schools.distinctive: One of only two schools naming 'the NHS' as a discrete question theme. Welsh-medium and bilingual interviews are available — a genuine localisation requirement if we build a Cardiff mode. Welsh-domiciled applicants receive additional consideration in the pre-interview scoring.
schools.confidence: HIGH on delivery and content themes; UNCERTAIN on personal statement; absent on structure

schools.structure: Same MMI model as A100; graduate-entry applicants go through the same selection process. Entry restricted to graduates (2:1 minimum) of four feeder programmes: BSc Medical Pharmacology Cardiff (B210), BSc Biomedical Sciences Cardiff (BC97), BMedSci Bangor (B100), BSc Medical Sciences University of South Wales (B901); qualifying dental graduates also eligible. Four years, joining Years 2-5. Next intake September 2027.
schools.distinctive: Cardiff's graduate entry is A101, NOT A104. A104 was Cardiff's historical 'Medicine with a Preliminary Year' code and is not in the current offering — correct this if it appears in our data.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM on format; UNCERTAIN on personal statement

schools.interview_type: MMI-style assessment day with long stations
schools.structure: Three face-to-face stations of 20 to 30 minutes each, run by a trained panel of clinicians, academics, medical students and members of the public. Station formats may include interviews, presentations or role play scenarios, and candidates may be questioned on personal statement content. Assessment day early in the New Year. GAMSAT or UCAT for home applicants.
schools.scientific_reasoning: not published (GAMSAT Paper 3 covers science pre-interview)
schools.distinctive: The longest stations in the UK by a wide margin — 20-30 minutes. Also the only school openly confirming presentations, roleplay AND application-based questioning in the same circuit. Swansea has no undergraduate-entry medicine.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM — structure on Swansea's own pages but not dated to a specific cycle

schools.structure: Face-to-face MMIs comprising six verbal stations with two questions per station, approximately one hour in total, in person at Bangor. Stations are discussion stations exploring personal qualities and attributes deemed important for doctors. A final score is determined by combining scores from each station; candidates ranked and highest scorers receive offers. Invitations issued in December; applicants book their own slots online.
schools.scientific_reasoning: partial (clinical reasoning listed on the FAQ page)
schools.distinctive: GMC status: progressing through approval to award a Primary Medical Qualification; accreditation completes only when the first cohort graduates, with Cardiff University as contingency awarding partner. Flag this to applicants. Two questions per station changes pacing — candidates must leave room for the second.
schools.changes: A100 full for September 2026 entry; 2027 applications opened 1 September 2026.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM — format HIGH from Bangor's own pages; station count from an FAQ page with no cycle stamp

schools.structure: Identical MMI structure to A100, plus an entrance examination for applicants not arriving via a recognised feeder stream. Delivered on the Medical Schools Council Assessment Alliance platform at Bangor: an MMI followed by the exam. The exam is 90 minutes, single-best-answer, testing Year 1 learning outcomes across 48 topic areas including cellular and molecular biology, anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, immunology and medical imaging principles.
schools.scoring_note: Exam pass mark standard-set with faculty and a psychometrician.
schools.distinctive: The only UK medical school in this dataset running a biomedical-science written examination at the interview stage. This is genuinely out of scope for an interview-practice product and should be explicitly excluded rather than half-served.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM

schools.structure: Candidates rotate around question stations. At each station two selectors explore one question area or domain for 5 minutes and score performance against pre-determined criteria. Five domain stations. No reading required during the interviews. Approximately one hour per candidate, in person at the Suttie Centre, Foresterhill.
schools.ethics: not a named MBChB station (Professionalism covers it)
published_criteria: Each station also independently scores communication and interpersonal skills
schools.scoring_note: Selection weighting: academic attainment/predictions 30%, UCAT 20%, interview 50%. Scoring criteria published verbatim: ability to express ideas freely and coherently; how well existing knowledge is used to formulate answers to unknown areas; ability to follow a reasoned argument and formulate an opinion; degree of preparedness; ability to discuss advantages and disadvantages of a problem; degree of motivation, commitment, reflection and sensitivity.
schools.distinctive: Two selectors per station and a communication score attached to EVERY station regardless of its domain — the same dual-track model our scoring should adopt. Aberdeen's Gateway2Medicine uses the same five domains.
schools.confidence: HIGH on format; MEDIUM on cycle (page still lists December 2025 dates)

schools.structure: Two stages. An observed preparatory group discussion in a group with five other applicants, discussing a specific scenario for around 30 minutes while observed by an assessor. Applicants then move to a separate room for a structured discussion with a different assessor. One hour forty minutes total including registration and welcome, with an optional 30-minute tour afterwards.
schools.delivery: in-person at Ninewells (UK); online via Blackboard Collaborate for international
schools.ethics: not published — 'a specific scenario' is unspecified
schools.independently_scored: different assessor per stage; method not described
published_criteria: Your ability to work within a group setting
schools.distinctive: DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS most commercial guides, which describe Dundee as an MMI school. It is a 30-minute observed group discussion followed by a one-to-one. Any Dundee-specific content we publish that assumes MMI is wrong.
schools.confidence: HIGH on format (institution page); page states September 2026 entry

schools.structure: Entry requirements page states only that no UCAT is required and 'an interview may be required'. No format, stations, duration or criteria published on any Gateway page.
schools.scoring_note: No UCAT required. UCAS deadline 1 July, not the 15 October medicine deadline.
schools.distinctive: Do not build a Dundee Gateway mode. There is nothing published to build it against.
schools.confidence: HIGH that Dundee publishes no Gateway interview detail

schools.route: undergraduate (graduate/mature applicants use the same route)
schools.interview_type: Assessment Day — multiple short interviews plus a group task
schools.structure: Shortlisted candidates attend an assessment half-day involving a series of short interviews. Scottish and RUK/RoI fee-rate candidates must attend in person. Edinburgh's own assessor-facing document (2025 entry, most recent published) describes each assessor running either three individual interviews of 12 minutes each in rotation, or supervising a group of three applicants in a 35-minute group task.
schools.delivery: in-person for Scottish/RUK/RoI (2027 entry); virtual in the 2025-entry document
schools.application_questioning: PS not formally assessed but may guide shortlisting and is 'essential preparation'
published_criteria: Assessments based on the core attributes required of medical doctors, outlined in the Medical Schools Council statement
schools.scoring_note: Scoring: academic 25%, UCAT total 17.5%, UCAT SJT band 7.5% (50% pre-assessment), Assessment Day 50%. SJT Band 4 or below the UCAT cut-off eliminates, except 'Plus Flag' applicants who are exempt from the UCAT threshold.
schools.distinctive: CORRECTS A WIDELY REPEATED ERROR: the claim that Edinburgh does not interview home applicants is out of date. Edinburgh is also the ONLY school in the entire dataset that has updated its wording to acknowledge the new UCAS three-question personal statement.
schools.changes: In-person requirement for Scottish/RUK/RoI on the 2027-entry page vs virtual delivery in the 2025-entry document; Edinburgh does not label this as a change.
schools.confidence: HIGH that interviews happen and on the weightings; MEDIUM/LOW on station counts and lengths (2025-entry assessor PDF)

schools.interview_type: panel / semi-structured — two panels in one 30-minute session (NOT MMI)
schools.structure: A 30-minute session divided into two sections, panel A and panel B. Panel A explores motivation to become a doctor, teamwork and related topics. Panel B focuses on communication and includes discussion of an ethical scenario: the applicant reads two brief scenarios of only two or three sentences and chooses one to discuss. Two interviewers. Interviewers have no knowledge of the applicant other than their name. Conversational, with no writing required at any stage.
schools.delivery: online (2027 entry, late November 2026 and March 2027)
published_criteria: Panel A — motivation to become a doctor, teamwork
schools.scoring_note: No interview score adjustments are made for any applicants, including widening participation candidates.
schools.distinctive: GLASGOW IS NOT AN MMI SCHOOL for 2027 entry. Any product content describing a Glasgow station circuit is wrong. The choose-one-of-two-ethical-scenarios mechanic is unique and directly buildable. Interviewers are blinded to everything but the name — application-defence practice is worthless here. Glasgow advises candidates to be aware of current issues and challenges within the NHS.
schools.confidence: HIGH — Glasgow's own page explicitly cites 2027 entry

schools.structure: Four mini interviews at different stations lasting about six minutes each. Assesses communication and interpersonal skills, critical thinking, reflection and ethical discussion. At least one station involves role-play and interaction with an actor. Applicants must demonstrate an understanding of medicine as a career and appreciate the realities of working in a caring profession.
schools.delivery: hybrid by fee status (in-person for Home-funded; online for all others)
published_criteria: Understanding of medicine as a career
Appreciation of the realities of a caring profession
schools.scoring_note: Hurdle-based process: 'your application will not be scored nor will weighting be applied'. ~650 interview places. Offers based on interview score and applicant route (Scotland / England / No Preference). UCAT is the tie-breaker.
schools.distinctive: Only four stations, so each carries 25% of the interview outcome — the highest per-station stakes in the dataset. At least one guaranteed actor station out of four means roleplay is 25%+ of the assessment here.
schools.confidence: HIGH on format; page states 2026 entry

schools.university: University of St Andrews with University of Dundee
schools.structure: A series of stations each lasting seven minutes, with 30-second breaks between. Candidates rotate starting at different points. Content covers motivation to study medicine, relevant work experience and personal attributes, and specifically why the applicant has applied to ScotGEM. Reflections on work experience form part of the discussion. Usually held at Ninewells Hospital, Dundee.
schools.scoring_note: Shortlisting ranked primarily on GAMSAT. ~160 interview places. Most decisions not made until mid-March 2027.
schools.distinctive: Explicitly assesses why the applicant chose ScotGEM specifically — a school-specific motivation requirement, like Sheffield's 'Knowledge of Sheffield' and Pears Cumbria's regional commitment. These three are the only genuine cases where content cannot be shared across schools.
schools.confidence: HIGH on station length; station COUNT unpublished on current and archived pages

schools.structure: Twelve-station circuit, clearly labelled 1-12: nine stations with interviewers and three rest stations. Four stations involve role players. Each station lasts 5 minutes with a one-minute warning; candidates get 1 minute to read the candidate instructions. Station 1 features an actor playing the part of a fellow student. Assessors use a structured marking sheet. Over an hour, in person at the Medical Biology Centre, Belfast.
schools.scoring_note: Only four competencies across nine assessed stations — so each competency is sampled more than twice. Explicitly states there are no stations requiring interpretation of data or graphs, and no writing at any station.
schools.distinctive: THE MOST ROLEPLAY-INTENSIVE CIRCUIT IN THE UK: four of nine assessed stations involve role players, i.e. 44% of the assessment. Station 1 is a peer roleplay (a fellow student), not a patient — this is exactly the kind of scenario a pre-medical applicant can legitimately handle and should be a template for our peer-conflict roleplays. Also publishes rest stations, which changes circuit pacing.
schools.confidence: HIGH; pages state 2026 entry

schools.structure: Seven online Zoom stations, five minutes in the station with a minute to read the information on screen. Two of the seven have role players; candidates are told it is the roleplayer they interact with, not the interviewer. No rest stations — rest time occurs between stations while the interviewer moves between breakout rooms. Just under an hour of interview; candidates told to allow two and a half hours.
schools.distinctive: Same four competencies, different circuit length — evidence that competency coverage, not station count, is the invariant. Design our content against competencies and parameterise the circuit.
schools.confidence: HIGH (QUB's own 2026-entry candidate guidance PDF)

schools.structure: Current pages state only that applicants must pass Multiple-Mini Interview assessment and demonstrate the personal qualities required of a doctor. The most recent published structural detail is Ulster's 2021-entry admissions feedback page: an eight-station MMI blueprint with one station per competency, delivered virtually. Communication Skills stations were the most discriminating and correlated maximally with overall applicant outcome. That source is five cycles old and is NOT confirmed for the target cycle.
schools.delivery: not published for current cycle; virtual in 2021 entry
published_criteria: Preparation and Motivation for a Medical Career
schools.scoring_note: GAMSAT minimum 50 in each section plus an overall threshold. Average overall GAMSAT of interviewed candidates 59 (2020-2025 data).
schools.distinctive: The 2021 finding that communication stations discriminated most strongly is the only published UK evidence of relative station validity we found. It supports weighting communication heavily in our own scoring — but it is one school, one cycle, five years ago.
schools.confidence: MEDIUM that the format is MMI; LOW for all structural detail (2021-entry source only)
